ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows: ABCD is a square, A is at the upper left, B is at the upper right, C is at the lower right, D is at the lower left; point E is above side AB, outside the square, and is connected to A and B; point F is below side DC, outside the square, and is connected to D and C. Therefore set coordinates according to the conventional direction in the figure: A=(0,13), B=(13,13), C=(13,0), D=(0,0). Let E=(x,13+h), where h>0. From AE=12, obtain x^2+h^2=144; from BE=5, obtain (x-13)^2+h^2=25. Subtract the two equations: x^2-(x-13)^2=119, so 26x-169=119, obtaining x=144/13. Substituting back gives h^2=144-(144/13)^2=3600/169, so h=60/13. Thus E=(144/13, 13+60/13). Let F=(u,-v), where v>0. From DF=5, obtain u^2+v^2=25; from CF=12, obtain (u-13)^2+v^2=144. Subtract the two equations: (u-13)^2-u^2=119, so -26u+169=119, obtaining u=25/13. Substituting back gives v^2=25-(25/13)^2=3600/169, so v=60/13. Thus F=(25/13,-60/13). Therefore the horizontal difference of EF is 144/13-25/13=119/13, and the vertical difference is 13+60/13+60/13=289/13. Therefore EF^2=(119/13)^2+(289/13)^2=(14161+83521)/169=97682/169=578.

raw_record.question_text: Square $ABCD$ has side length $13$, and points $E$ and $F$ are exterior to the square such that $BE=DF=5$ and $AE=CF=12$. Find $EF^{2}$.

method.method_draft: Use analytic coordinates. Read the diagram to place the square in the usual orientation with A=(0,13), B=(13,13), C=(13,0), D=(0,0), with E above AB and F below DC. Let E=(x,13+h), h>0. From AE=12 and BE=5, solve x^2+h^2=144 and (x-13)^2+h^2=25, giving x=144/13 and h=60/13. Let F=(u,-v), v>0. From DF=5 and CF=12, solve u^2+v^2=25 and (u-13)^2+v^2=144, giving u=25/13 and v=60/13. Then EF^2=(144/13-25/13)^2+(13+60/13+60/13)^2=(119/13)^2+(289/13)^2=578.

method.method_draft: Use vector addition along the broken path E→A→D→F. Since AE=12, BE=5, and AB=13, triangle ABE is a 5-12-13 right triangle with right angle at E. Similarly, triangle DFC is a 5-12-13 right triangle with right angle at F. Let p=vector E→A, q=vector A→D, and r=vector D→F. Then EF vector is p+q+r, with lengths |p|=12, |q|=13, |r|=5. From triangle ABE and the fact AD is perpendicular to AB, compute p·q=60. From triangle DFC and the fact AD is perpendicular to DC, compute q·r=60. Also the direction of AE has slope ratio 5:12 while the direction of DF has reciprocal perpendicular ratio 12:5 on the opposite side, so p·r=0. Therefore EF^2=|p+q+r|^2=12^2+13^2+5^2+2(60+60+0)=578.
